method: OpenStreetMap way 289305285 ('913 - ASG Ring' [sic], place=locality, wikidata Q438407 linking to the Alternating Gradient Synchrotron), a single closed way of 20 nodes, used verbatim. Building 913 is independently confirmed as 'AGS Ring' (map coordinate H3) by BNL's own central-campus-map building key (src:geo-bnl-central-campus-map). Kept accuracy_m at the ring-road/imagery-traced tier (≥30 m) and confidence 'approximate' despite a passing length check: the way carries place=locality rather than a tunnel/building/man_made tag, i.e. it reads as a hand-drawn boundary around the visible ring feature in aerial imagery, not an official technical alignment (contrast geometry:bnl-rhic-ring's explicit tunnel=yes/indoor=yes tagging). This mirrors the CERN SPS ring precedent (GEOMETRY_cern.md conflict #1).
name: Alternating Gradient Synchrotron ring, full ring
notes: QA pass (2026-09-21): removed the `valid: {start: '1960-07', end: null}` window a previous pass set (1960-07 is AGS's own operational start, already `accelerator:ags`'s sourced interval start -- `valid` here was redundant with the entity's own timeline, not a case of the shape's lifetime differing from it). Removing it is a preventive fix for a latent bug in hepgraph.atlas.build._feature_segments(): any `valid` dict with a non-null `start` and `end: null` hard-codes `status: 'active'` through build day regardless of the entity's real status, bypassing state_segments entirely. Currently harmless only because AGS genuinely is still active; the same pattern produced a live false-'active' claim on geometry:hera-tunnel-ring and geometry:bnl-rhic-ring (both decommissioned machines), fixed the same way in this pass -- see docs/atlas-worklog/REVIEW_geometry_qa.md. Confirmed via hepgraph.atlas.build._Context.status_at_build on accelerator:ags at build day 2026-09-21: 'active', matching accelerator:ags.status.
